subject: Can I use stat_smooth with weighted data?

messages.author: 7205147d8a925676
messages.subject: Can I use stat_smooth with weighted data?
parts:
In general, I've been able to get things to work as I'd like by adding
weight=value to most functions. In particular, using:

df <- read.csv("data",header=FALSE)
df <- df[0:40]
colnames(df) <- c(1:40)
rownames(df) <- c(2:9)
df <- namerows(df,col.name="n")
mdf <- melt(df)
ggplot(mdf, aes(x=variable, group=n,weight=value)) + facet_grid(. ~ n)
+ coord_flip() + geom_freqpoly()
ggplot(mdf, aes(x=variable, group=n,weight=value)) + facet_grid(. ~ n)
+ coord_flip() + geom_density(fill="grey50")

I was able to get
http://ggplot2.googlegroups.com/web/stacked_graph.png?gda=I7uaiUMAAAAGA9Vtd7sQB1bI8Dxk8wQo8tCdS7f8RPWQMEJi64ANcq0Cfnk1G8rBf6oGy9O_LssytiJ-HdGYYcPi_09pl8N7FWLveOaWjzbYnpnkpmxcWg&gsc=RlSNHQsAAADqnOn9KDmIdH-Z26_1ubGK

Now I'd like to layer a graph of the averages, with error bars, onto
that, and the stat_smooth examples look like what I want, but I can't
get any meaningful output by specifying weight=value. Do I really want
to use stat_smooth, or should I be using something else? If I should
be using stat_smooth, how should I use it?

Thanks,
Daniel

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Can I use stat_smooth with weighted data?
parts:
Hi Daniel,

The weights are passed on to stat_smooth, but I'm not sure how the
individual modelling functions use them. Could you please provide a
reproducible example that illustrates your problem?

Hadley
